behavior: A distinct RF-owned AFTER row trigger registers withdrawal writes with the existing company archive generation protocol. The frozen historical ten-trigger inventory is unchanged; archive completion and cancellation policy are unchanged.

Actual writes invalidate prior-generation receipts and in-flight exports in the same year. Exact withdrawal replay, INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and rolled-back writes do not advance the committed generation.

First installation enumerates retained scopes under an exclusive table lock and owner-only transactional FORCE-RLS suspension. A correctly installed tracker makes migration replay stable; absent, disabled or conditional trackers trigger retained-scope invalidation.
Temporary role membership and tracker creation grants are restored exactly. The existing unconditional BEFORE company guard is required. Withdrawal EXECUTE remains unavailable to runtime callers.
Application rollback retains tracking; it neither deletes withdrawals nor makes older generation receipts current.

review.result: No remaining material findings in final generation migration/rollback/tests and native-probe source.
review.findingFixed: Initial installed-trigger detection omitted conditional/constraint trigger attributes; final code requires exact unconditional ordinary immediate row-trigger shape, and tests conditional tracker/company-guard cases.

nativeProtocolProbe.scope: Entire generation migration and exact existing archive tracking/company-lock/scope-lock functions on native PostgreSQL 17 with minimal RF table, synthetic RLS policy and restricted fixture migrator. Tests generation, first activation, migration replay, no-op insert, rollback, conditional-trigger drift, temporary grant removal and role/ACL/RLS restoration. Not actual withdrawal append, Supabase authorization, complete migration chain, immutable receipt integrity or export/race execution.
checks: first activation invalidates only retained scope
temporary SET memberships and tracker grant restored exactly
FORCE RLS restored and still hides rows without synthetic actor
migration replay preserves generations and authority
restricted owner insert fires tracker after execute grant revoked
conditional tracker does not suppress retained-scope invalidation
disabled tracker repaired and invalidated once
conditional company guard refusal rolls back borrowed authority
retained scope without generation row initialized once
empty activation does not invalidate unrelated generations
application rollback retains tracking and generations

limits: Twenty real database cases were collected only. Actual RF withdrawal append, full Supabase migration chain, immutable receipt integrity, real authorization/RLS and export-completion races require full CI execution.

The 14 native PostgreSQL checks use exact public tracking/locking functions and the entire new migration with a minimal RF table and synthetic scope policy. They prove the specified protocol/role/trigger behaviors, not complete application readiness.

An old-format exporter begun after withdrawal can still omit withdrawal history and mint a current-generation receipt. The existing completion RPC also lacks a READ COMMITTED requirement; old repeatable-read snapshots can miss a generation change after acquiring the company lock. Neither gap is fixed by generation tracking.

Archive-owner verified-byte coverage/completion and Company Access eligibility remain pending the explicit architecture decision. No future-facade change, withdrawal activation, external effect or launch authority follows.
